title: The coskeleton term represents compatible truncated simplex families
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with finite limits [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits], let $K$ be a simplicial object of $\mathcal C$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object], and let $n\geq1$. Put $V=\mathrm{sk}_{n-1}K$. There exists an $(n-1)$-coskeleton $(L,\varepsilon)$ of $V$, with $\varepsilon:\mathrm{sk}_{n-1}L\to V$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton]. For every object $W$ of $\mathcal C$, the map sending $h:W\to L_n$ to the family $(\varepsilon_k\circ h_\alpha)_\alpha$, where $h_\alpha:W\to L_k$ is $L(\alpha)\circ h$ (so the family is $(\varepsilon_k\circ L(\alpha)\circ h)_\alpha$) and $\alpha:[k]\to[n]$ ranges over all order-preserving maps with $k\leq n-1$, is a natural bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(W,L_n)$ to compatible families $(x_\alpha:W\to K_k)_\alpha$ satisfying $K(\psi)\circ x_\alpha=x_{\alpha\circ\psi}$ whenever $\psi:[k']\to[k]$ is order-preserving and $\alpha:[k]\to[n]$ is as above. For the canonical morphism $c:K\to L$, the corresponding family for $c_n$ is $(K(\alpha))_\alpha$.

source.place: Simplicial, Lemma 0183 (lemma-existence-cosk): the coskeleton cosk_{n-1} of an (n-1)-truncated simplicial object exists when the category has finite limits, with maps W -> L_n corresponding to compatible families over all order-preserving alpha : [k] -> [n], k <= n-1 (the node states this 0183 form; the earlier text named 0186). The comparison with the face tuples of 0186 is lem-weil-pbc-matching-object-proper-faces.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-truncated-coskeleton-finite-limits] (1) to $m=n-1$ and $U=V=\mathrm{sk}_{n-1}K$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton]. It gives an $(n-1)$-coskeleton $(L,\varepsilon)$ with $L_j=\lim V(j)$ and an isomorphism $\varepsilon:\mathrm{sk}_{n-1}L\to V$. The indexing category has one object for each order-preserving $\alpha:[k]\to[j]$ with $k\leq n-1$, and an arrow $\alpha'\to\alpha$ for each order-preserving $\psi:[k']\to[k]$ with $\alpha'=\alpha\circ\psi$. Write $p_{j,\alpha}:L_j\to K_k$ for its cone projections. The stated description of the simplicial maps induced by postcomposition gives $p_{k,\mathrm{id}}\circ L(\alpha)=p_{n,\alpha}$ for $\alpha:[k]\to[n]$. For $k\leq n-1$, $\mathrm{id}_{[k]}$ is terminal in $(\Delta/[k])_{\leq n-1}$: every $\beta:[j]\to[k]$ has the unique arrow $\beta\to\mathrm{id}_{[k]}$ given by $\beta$. Hence it is initial in the opposite indexing category and $p_{k,\mathrm{id}}:L_k\to K_k$ is an isomorphism, with inverse determined by the cone $(K(\beta):K_k\to K_j)_\beta$. For $\psi:[k']\to[k]$ between degrees at most $n-1$, the induced-map equation and the cone equation give $p_{k',\mathrm{id}}\circ L(\psi)=p_{k,\psi}=K(\psi)\circ p_{k,\mathrm{id}}$. Thus $p_{.,\mathrm{id}}:\mathrm{sk}_{n-1}L\to V$ is a natural isomorphism. Put $a=\varepsilon\circ p_{.,\mathrm{id}}^{-1}$, a natural automorphism of $V$. Then $\varepsilon_k\circ L(\alpha)\circ h=a_k\circ p_{n,\alpha}\circ h$ for every $h:W\to L_n$.

source.place: Lemma 0183 (lemma-existence-cosk), finite-limit formula and the induced simplicial maps

proof.text: By the defining universal property of the limit [def-galois-finite-limits-colimits], $h\mapsto(p_{n,\alpha}\circ h)_\alpha$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(W,L_n)$ to cones over $V(n)$. A family $(x_\alpha:W\to K_k)_\alpha$ is such a cone exactly when $K(\psi)\circ x_\alpha=x_{\alpha\circ\psi}$ for each order-preserving $\psi:[k']\to[k]$. Since $a$ from Step 1 is a natural automorphism of $V$, $K(\psi)\circ a_k=a_{k'}\circ K(\psi)$; therefore $(x_\alpha)_\alpha\mapsto(a_k\circ x_\alpha)_\alpha$ maps compatible families bijectively to compatible families, with inverse given by $a^{-1}$. The equation at the end of Step 1 shows that the composite bijection sends $h$ to $(\varepsilon_k\circ L(\alpha)\circ h)_\alpha$. Both the limit bijection and postcomposition by $a$ commute with precomposition by $g:W'\to W$, so their composite is natural in $W$.

source.place: Lemma 0183 (lemma-existence-cosk), proof, maps into the limit as compatible families

proof.text: Let $c:K\to L$ be the canonical morphism [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton]. Its defining equation $\varepsilon\circ\mathrm{sk}_{n-1}c=\mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{sk}_{n-1}K}$ gives $\varepsilon_k\circ c_k=\mathrm{id}_{K_k}$ for $k\leq n-1$. For every $\alpha:[k]\to[n]$, simplicial naturality [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] gives $L(\alpha)\circ c_n=c_k\circ K(\alpha)$. Thus the $\alpha$-component of the family of $c_n$ is $\varepsilon_k\circ L(\alpha)\circ c_n=\varepsilon_k\circ c_k\circ K(\alpha)=K(\alpha)$. The family is compatible because $K$ is a contravariant functor: $K(\psi)\circ K(\alpha)=K(\alpha\circ\psi)$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_coskeleton_matching_tuples {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasFiniteLimits C] (K : SimplicialObject C) (n : ℕ) (_hn : 1 ≤ n) : let m := n - 1 let i := SimplexCategory.Truncated.inclusion m let V := (truncation m).obj K let F := fun W : C ↦ {x : ∀ (k : SimplexCategory.Truncated m), (i.obj k ⟶ SimplexCategory.mk n) → (W ⟶ K.obj (op (i.obj k))) // ∀ (k' k : SimplexCategory.Truncated m) (ψ : k' ⟶ k) (α : i.obj k ⟶ SimplexCategory.mk n), x k α ≫ K.map (i.map ψ).op = x k' (i.map ψ ≫ α)} ∃ (L : SimplicialObject C) (ε : (truncation m).obj L ⟶ V), L.IsRightKanExtension ε ∧ ∃ (c : K ⟶ L), (truncation m).map c ≫ ε = 𝟙 V ∧ ∃ (e : ∀ W : C, (W ⟶ L _⦋n⦌) ≃ F W), (∀ (W : C) (h : W ⟶ L _⦋n⦌) (k : SimplexCategory.Truncated m) (α : i.obj k ⟶ SimplexCategory.mk n), (e W h).val k α = h ≫ L.map α.op ≫ ε.app (op k)) ∧ (∀ (W' W : C) (g : W' ⟶ W) (h : W ⟶ L _⦋n⦌) (k : SimplexCategory.Truncated m) (α : i.obj k ⟶ SimplexCategory.mk n), (e W' (g ≫ h)).val k α = g ≫ (e W h).val k α) ∧ (∀ (k : SimplexCategory.Truncated m) (α : i.obj k ⟶ SimplexCategory.mk n), (e (K _⦋n⦌) (c.app (op (SimplexCategory.mk n)))).val k α = K.map α.op)
